name: RxnOptBench
description: DRAFT: this candidate has not been published. Distribution URLs using main are intended future locations; main currently serves an earlier release. Local hashes and local-loader validation do not establish remote availability. Public source-category/license evidence has been organized; historical acquisition and API hosting are unknown, and SI/intermediate-expression scope remains unresolved. A local target-policy candidate with 4,773 constructed reaction-condition QA records in eight test subsets, derived from human-reviewed published screening tables. Source experimental measurements are literature-derived. The separate broader candidate contains 777 source-relevant reviewed records from the final 232 source groups; those records are outside these eight RecordSets. Exact final-question regeneration is not claimed. Unverified dr/rr axes are retained as raw metadata and excluded from scoring. Best scores use declared released observational support rather than an unrestricted chemical optimum. Each Croissant record exposes its full candidate JSON record as lossless UTF-8 Text (json_record) in a derived gzipped TSV, plus searchable identifiers. Decode json_record with a JSON parser to recover nested inputs, candidates, answers, and provenance; record_schema.json documents all nested fields. Identifiers are unique within their subset, not across all eight subsets.
conditionsOfAccess: The selected candidate data terms are the RxnOptBench Noncommercial Research License v1.0 for rights the authors hold; code uses MIT. Upstream material retains its original license and permissions; see UPSTREAM_LICENSE_NOTICES.md at the intended data host. This candidate is local and unpublished. Intended access is a Hugging Face account and acceptance of a lightweight noncommercial research-use agreement with automatic approval, as configured for the earlier release at this repository. Public code/metadata live at https://github.com/SII-gelingli/RxnOptBench; their current main revision does not establish availability of this candidate. The provided load/validation script uses an authorized cached Hugging Face login or HF_TOKEN to download and hash-check transport files, then supplies them to mlcroissant using its standard local mapping API. The reference loader itself does not read HF_TOKEN for arbitrary HTTP FileObjects. Acceptance of the access agreement is still required.

rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark measures selection among candidates derived from disclosed literature screening tables. A best answer is best within the explicitly declared released observational support under the utility, not a global optimum over chemical space. No direct wet-lab guidance, autonomous experimentation, safety/cost assessment, or open-ended synthesis ability is validated.

The current candidate retains 4,773 questions in eight subsets and 552 parent tables. Their union represents 4,768 distinct released observed rows, whereas the paper describes 5,451 source-table entries; 298 parent tables have all reported source rows represented and 254 do not. global_best_scope is all_released_observations_for_parent_table. A best label does not certify the optimum over unavailable original rows. Individual MC and FIB questions expose different observed supports.

The fixed-target dr/rr policy requires source-identified components, a target fixed across the table, and a human-verified component-to-target mapping. No such independent mapping ledger was found in the current workspace; the author confirmed there are no additional records to use. All 65 observed parent-table/axis combinations therefore have status exclude_unverified. Their original parsed dr/rr observations remain in raw_observed_scores or raw_observed_score, while dr/rr values in the score-bearing structure are null and do not affect utility or gold labels. No major:minor normalization is used for these excluded axes. Other existing score factors retain their declared treatment. This is a conservative exclusion policy, not a claim that target mappings have been verified.

Fill-in-the-blank candidate values are individually source-derived, but their Cartesian product contains unobserved joint tuples. A structurally valid tuple that does not match a released observed row is a non-Hit outside measured support, not a chemically invalid reaction or a measured failure. Score conditioned on Hit excludes those unobserved tuples.

Question inputs, candidate indices, and reference/control contexts are preserved for rescoring archived predictions. Gold labels and relative scores may change under the corrected policy. Some reference rows become best after exclusion, and a small number of question variants contain ties across all options; unchanged contexts are not evidence that the corrected optimum was withheld. Reference rows and candidate rows are disjoint by source-row identity, which does not guarantee distinct full condition tuples when different source rows repeat the same conditions. The local audit reports affected items separately. Historical generations were not rerun under altered prompts.

Paired reference/control subsets match candidate sets, but their released option order differs for many items. Historical provider-input ordering has not been independently verified from complete prompt-order logs. These paired comparisons therefore do not isolate a causal effect of adding reference outcomes; candidate-set matching must not be described as complete prompt identity apart from the reference field.

Deterministic rescoring of retained model predictions does not reproduce historical hosted-model generations or establish invariance across endpoint versions, backends, decoding settings, or time. Submitted historical aggregates and corrected-policy results are separately versioned and must not be interchanged.

Sources are recent organic-methodology literature across 16 selected journals, including publisher-confirmed first publications in 2026. They must not be described as exclusively first published in 2025. A Crossref year can reflect a later issue date rather than first online publication; not all records with a 2026 registry date are asserted to be 2026 first publications. Expert review compared accepted chemical records with source material. Source exposure and model training cutoffs are not fully observable; absence of training contamination has not been established.

This Croissant file describes only the eight evaluation subsets. The current broader candidate separately inventories available construction/evaluation code, six task prompts, 777 reviewed records conservatively limited to the final 232 source groups, review tooling, validators, and archived model outputs. Those files are not additional Croissant RecordSets here. The retained bridge covers 416 final tables; 12 final source groups have no matching reviewed record and are not filled with invented mappings. Unreleased molecular-recognition components and their model-specific postprocessing, model weights, publisher PDFs, and source images are excluded. A historical construction experiment produced 4,473 questions from an earlier full 884-record review snapshot. That experiment does not describe the current 777-record scope: construction has not been rerun for the reduced snapshot, and exact regeneration of the final 4,773 questions is not claimed. Exact review-snapshot-to-final-question lineage remains incomplete; complete final-dataset or raw-PDF-to-benchmark regeneration is not established.

meta.doi contains frozen source-identifier strings. The MC-all file has 552 parent tables and 236 case-sensitive raw source strings; four case-variant groups reduce this to 232 case-insensitive source groups. A separate public bibliographic audit matched their 232 DOI identifiers to Crossref. Frozen strings remain unchanged. Registry matching establishes identity, not permission to redistribute source material.

Public source-category/license evidence has been organized for 232 final-source DOIs across six publisher families. The HF candidate metadata/source_rights/ inventory distinguishes article and SI evidence, conditional routes and unknown scope; it does not declare project-wide clearance. The current reviewed-record scope is limited to 777 records associated with those final source groups. This source relevance filter does not establish item-level license clearance or resolve expression in explanatory notes. Historical acquisition dates, institutional subscription details and API hosting are unknown. Actual source-file correspondence and some SI/third-party scope remain unresolved. UPSTREAM_LICENSE_NOTICES.md explains that the authors' data terms grant only their own rights and do not reduce permissions independently granted by upstream licenses.
rai:dataBiases: Methodology papers disclose curated evidence supporting a narrative rather than complete optimization histories. Successful, interesting, or publishable transformations and selected comparison rows may be overrepresented. This benchmark cannot recover undisclosed experiments.

The selected journals, recent-literature sampling frame, extraction feasibility, and human curation produce uneven coverage of reaction classes, substrates, catalysts, condition fields, and table formats. Tables that could not be structured reliably or lacked usable reaction/outcome information are underrepresented.

Reference/control contexts were constructed using the historical utility and retained unchanged when labels were corrected. Their context-selection distribution need not match a chemist's available information. Corrected-optimal reference rows, repeated condition tuples across distinct source rows, all-option ties, and unmatched candidate orders are reported as limitations rather than evidence of a causal reference benefit.

The aggregate utility prioritizes reported yield and retained selectivity factors. Missing factors, source reporting conventions, and the conservative exclusion of unverified dr/rr axes can affect rankings. It does not encode every target-isomer preference, safety constraint, cost, or chemical objective.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Test records describe chemical reactions, conditions, outcomes, and source identifiers. No personal, demographic, medical, political, or other human-sensitive attributes are intentionally collected as benchmark features. Public author information appears in documentation. The paper reports aggregate information about six paid chemistry interns; individual annotator identities are not test-set attributes.
rai:dataUseCases: Offline comparison of reaction-condition recommendation systems within a fixed, source-derived candidate space. Report MC Accuracy/relative Score and distinguish FIB observed-row Hit, Strict Accuracy, and Score conditioned on Hit. State dataset and scoring-policy versions and use subset plus id as the question key.

The evaluated construct is comparative selection among disclosed conditions for the same reaction, based on source-reviewed rows and reported measurements. It is conditional on released support and the declared utility, not unrestricted chemical optimization or laboratory readiness.

All eight subsets are test-only. Training or fine-tuning on these records compromises evaluation on them; no disjoint training/validation split or established fine-tuning benefit is supplied. Direct experimental deployment and outcome inference for unobserved tuples have not been validated.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Structured aggregation of published conditions can aid reproducible comparison while reducing the effort needed to retrieve and reuse chemical information. This creates misuse risk and a risk that offline scores are mistaken for experimental readiness. Documentation retains provenance and explains disclosed-row, target-policy and sampling limits. Intended access uses a noncommercial research-use agreement with automatic approval; this provides accountability and friction, not proof of safe use or source rights. The current candidate is unpublished. Public source-category evidence has been organized, while unknown historical acquisition/API-hosting details and unresolved SI and intermediate-expression scope prevent a blanket clearance claim. The earlier repository's access configuration does not certify this candidate's readiness.
rai:dataCollection: Sources are recent organic-methodology papers and supporting information from 16 selected journals, including publisher-confirmed first publications in 2026. Available code has local PDF/table-processing stages and API-dependent stages. Historical download dates, institutional subscriptions and whether those API services were locally hosted or external are unknown; code capability does not prove historical transmission. Four semi-automated stages detect and structure screening tables, followed by final human verification against source material before question construction. Public source-category/license evidence is inventoried separately, without asserting that all acquisition, processing or redistribution conditions are established. Experimental outcomes are literature-derived, not simulated or newly measured. hasSyntheticData is true only for the programmatically constructed QA layer, including masking, candidate arrangement, context construction and computed annotations.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Four master's-level and two doctoral-level paid chemistry interns compared extracted tables with source PDFs, corrected fields, and accepted, rejected, or skipped tables using an internal review interface. The paper reports RMB 300/day for master's-level interns and RMB 400/day for doctoral-level interns. No independent multi-label annotation or inter-annotator-agreement statistic is claimed. General acceptance of a table is distinct from an independently documented dr/rr target-component mapping. No such mapping record was found; unverified dr/rr axes are excluded from scoring and preserved as raw metadata.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Internal per-table expert-review interface described in the paper. An available implementation and the current 777 source-relevant reviewed records are inventoried in the broader candidate, outside these eight Croissant evaluation RecordSets. Individual independent dr/rr target-mapping verification is not established.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The 0.2.6-target-policy candidate preserves question inputs, candidates, indices, source strings, and reference/control contexts from the compatible historical evaluation snapshot. It retains all provided raw observations, nulls unverified score-bearing dr/rr fields, and recomputes effective/relative scores and gold/tie sets under a consistent released-support policy. No measured yields or selectivities are invented. Separate versioned policy, relabel, per-question change, and historical-scoring manifests document the transformation. JSONL and native JSON represent equivalent records; lossless TSV.gz exists solely for standard Croissant-loader compatibility. Archived index-restored predictions are rescored against unchanged retained question inputs. Derived response artifacts and post-hoc index restoration do not independently verify original provider prompt ordering or reproduce provider calls. The separate broader candidate has been conservatively scoped to 777 source-relevant reviewed records without changing the 4,773 evaluation questions or their scores. An earlier 884-record full-snapshot construction experiment yielded 4,473 questions; no reduced-snapshot rerun or exact review-to-final regeneration is asserted.
